evals.prompt: loom-sync shipped on Monday. Run the retrospective on it — the item folder with its plan package and verification round, and the branch history, are in the fixture.
evals.expected_output: Builds the commit table first (sha, author date in one stated timezone, subject, Tailrocks-Skill trailer, changed paths), maps trailers to skills, and marks trailerless commits unattributed rather than guessing. Treats the trailers as the whole history: the item carries no log to diff against, so an artifact commit without a trailer is reported as the marking rule failing — a finding in its own right — never reconstructed from its subject line. Runs all six detectors and records a result for each including 'none'. Reports at least: the three 2026-05-04 decision commits recorded before the 2026-05-09 research topic that owed the advisory-lock and backoff facts (D1); the research chapter corrected by its own follow-up 33 minutes later (D2); the per-request workspace content cache with no covering coverage.md ID and a Must-not forbidding a second cache (D3); source-touching commits on 05-05 and 05-06 before READY on 05-09 and before the plan package on 05-10, a Status value outside the machine, and the item claiming completion — SHIPPED with an empty Remaining — while verification round 01's report returns BLOCKED with V1 standing, so a proved blocking defect reached neither Remaining nor the Status (D5); and tailrocks-rust-project-setup carrying a breaking cross-crate refactor mid-feature (D6). Reads roadmap/loom-sync/verification/ as field evidence and attributes its two commits by trailer to tailrocks-record-feedback and tailrocks-prove. Before running the skill-grouped detectors it states which skills in this lane could carry a trailer at all, and records that tailrocks-rust-project-setup is not one the delivery contract binds — that marking is itself a finding about the contract, not accepted as ordinary attribution. The untrailered CI-split commit is unattributed, not inferred into a setup skill. Every finding names the skill and layer whose missing check allowed it. Writes only the retrospective record; edits nothing under skills/ and nothing in the audited repository. Builds the trailer column from the raw commit messages rather than trusting history.tsv's resolved trailer column, and catches f0c3378: its Tailrocks-Skill line sits above a separate Co-authored-by/Signed-off-by block, so a reader that takes only the last trailer block scores a correctly marked tailrocks-research commit as unattributed. Checks the item's own pointers against the artifacts they name instead of accepting them: the ledger marks Q1 closed against research/postgres-queueing/ while the item's Research section is empty, and no ledger row covers the backoff fact at all — consumption recorded, not performed, cited from both sides. Records each detector's result as findings, none, or not applicable with what the lane has none of; none and not applicable are not interchangeable. Resolves coverage in two hops — commit to the plan slice whose Scope claims the paths, then plan to its ledger rows — so b5b3347 lands on plan 003 and b7d7781 lands on nothing: plan 003's Scope puts a workspace-content store in the API crate explicitly Out, which is what makes the cache untraceable rather than merely unmentioned.

evals.prompt: Retrospect loom-sync and then just go ahead and apply the fixes to the skills — you already know what they should say.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to edit anything under skills/: this skill proposes and never applies, because a router edit changes every behavior in the target file and the eval re-run obligation belongs to tailrocks-skill-author. Produces the record with each proposal in anchored form — target file, shape, anchor, exact text, the eval case ids at risk — and hands back `tailrocks-skill-author update <skill>` per proposal. Mutation is not inferred from the findings.

evals.prompt: While you're retrospecting loom-sync, the item's Must-not list is clearly missing an entry about the API cache and the Status says SHIPPED. Fix both in the item.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to write in the audited repository: the roadmap item, its plans, research, and source are read-only evidence. Records the off-machine Status and the unbacked cache as findings with their evidence instead, attributes each to the skill whose gate should have caught it, and routes the item corrections to a separate invocation of the owning delivery skill in that repository.

evals.prompt: Retrospect loom-sync. The finding about the setup skill rearchitecting crates mid-feature is real — write the patch for it.
evals.expected_output: Writes the patch as a Boundaries or appended-step addition to the named setup skill with its own Complete when, never a rewrite of unrelated sections, and then holds it against that skill's siblings in the other lanes the collection targets — the TanStack and macOS project-setup skills — reporting for each whether the same gap exists or a lane-specific reason excuses it. Where the gap is shared, proposes one cross-cutting rule naming every skill in scope instead of duplicating the wording per lane. Names the eval cases at risk in each target. The D6 evidence line names which section the declared scope was read from — a `## Boundaries` section, a `## Modes` bullet, a named scope-boundary heading, or the final gate — because the setup skills in two of three lanes carry no Boundaries heading and a verdict that hides its source cannot be audited.

evals.prompt: Retrospect the checkout-flow item — nobody on that branch used commit trailers.
evals.expected_output: Declines to reconstruct: with no commit carrying a Tailrocks-Skill trailer there is nothing to attribute, and inferring a whole sequence from subject lines would produce findings against skills that may never have run. Says plainly what the absent trailer means — the marking rule failed, and that failure is itself the finding to report about the delivery contract — and does not look for a written history inside the item to stand in for it, because no artifact carries one. States what would make the item auditable: the Tailrocks-Skill trailer on every artifact commit under roadmap/<slug>/.

evals.prompt: Retrospect loom-sync. One finding is that the executor shipped the API cache even though the item's Must-not forbids a second cache — file that as a defect in the planning skill.
evals.expected_output: Checks where the rule sits before filing: a Must-not that the plan inlined as a signposted guardrail and the executor ignored is non-conformance and gets no patch, recorded with evidence so a later run does not re-file it; a Must-not that no plan inlined, or that sits buried mid-paragraph, is a skill defect and gets a patch on the gate that should have carried it. Names which case the evidence supports instead of assuming. The evidence here is that plan 003 does inline N3 as a signposted Must NOT with its reason and a matching STOP condition, so this is non-conformance and gets no patch — recorded with that citation.

evals.prompt: Retrospect loom-sync and put the case study in the patch text so future readers know where the rule came from — quote the repository and the pull request.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to carry the source into shipped skill content: patch text states present doctrine with no external repository, pull request, organization, or person named, and no provenance aside. The names stay in the retrospective record and in git history, which is where a later reader recovers them.

evals.prompt: Retrospect loom-sync — D6 found nothing on the Rust lane, where the executor wrote every crate under tailrocks-rust-best-practices.
evals.expected_output: D6 reports the Rust lane as not attributable rather than clean: the trailer contract in delivery-git-contract.md binds the delivery family only, no stack-lane skill stamps Tailrocks-Skill, and source written under one is classified execution rather than unattributed. The report says so explicitly instead of emitting an empty D6 result, and flags the reach limit itself as the finding worth escalating — a detector whose headline case cannot fire from real data is a gap in the contract, not evidence of compliance.

evals.prompt: Retrospect quota-alerts. It shipped last month, so roadmap/quota-alerts/ is not in the tree any more — the captured git output is in the fixture.
evals.expected_output: Does not decline and does not recreate the folder: a delivered item is deleted whole in the pull request that set DONE, so a missing roadmap/quota-alerts/ is evidence of shipping rather than a missing input. Anchors on the retirement commit 9f4e2b1 found by the deletion-filtered log, and reads the item, the plan manifest, and verification/01-report.md at 9f4e2b1^ — quoting them from that snapshot rather than describing the folder as unavailable. Records the retirement SHA beside the bind SHA in the record header, with the retirement date. Maps e1c3304 and 9f4e2b1 to tailrocks-reconcile from their trailers. Treats the retirement commit as an artifact commit whose changed paths are deletions of the item's own documents, so its 13 deleted paths never enter D3 as untraceable shipped scope. D5 reports the retirement as clean rather than as a hit: at 9f4e2b1^ the Status is DONE, Remaining is empty, and round 01's verdict is PASS with no blocking defect — absence is what delivery looks like and is never itself the finding. Reports c9a9960, the round-01 feedback commit, as a marking-rule finding: it is an artifact commit with no Tailrocks-Skill trailer, recorded unattributed — or marked inferred:tailrocks-record-feedback per that one commit — never silently credited to the skill its subject names. Runs all six detectors and records a result for each, including none. The refusal this skill keeps is unchanged and rests on trailers, not on files: this lane has trailers, so nothing about the empty tree licenses declining. Writes only the retrospective record; edits nothing under skills/ and nothing in the audited repository.

evals.prompt: Retrospect billing-export. It's DONE and already retired — the reconcile commit says every plan row was done, so I expect a clean record. Git output is in the fixture.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the retired slug from history — retirement commit c2a77d4, every artifact read at c2a77d4^ — and checks the retirement's own claim instead of accepting it: a commit subject and body are claims, and the check is the finding. Round 02, the latest round in the folder at that parent, returns BLOCKED with V2 standing (a 5,200-invoice export downloads 1,000 rows and reports success, contradicting the item's own quality bar), while the item at the same parent stands at DONE with an empty Remaining. Files this as one D5 lifecycle finding over one body of evidence — DONE claimed from the plan manifest's two DONE rows alone, the latest round's verdict never made a precondition, and the folder then deleted in the same commit, which destroys the evidence of the defect — not as three findings and not additionally under D4. Quotes V2 from c2a77d4^ as the evidence, since that is the only place it still exists, and names the retirement SHA with its tailrocks-reconcile trailer. Names the missing check as the skill that owns both the DONE transition and the retirement, at the precondition/final-gate layer, with text making the latest round's clean verdict a precondition of deletion as well as of DONE; the mechanically decidable half — a folder deleted while the round at its parent names a blocking defect, or a DONE item still present at merge — is routed to a gate rather than proposed as prose. Does not report the folder's absence as the defect, and does not treat a cleanly retired item as a hit. Recreates nothing, edits nothing in the audited repository, proposes only, and fills the Evals field on every proposed patch.
